name: Fair Fares NYC (half-price MetroCard)
offers: 50% off subway, eligible bus and Access-A-Ride fares.
hours_notes: Apply online, then upload documents in the ACCESS HRA app.
eligibility: NYC residents 18-64 with low income. Immigration status not asked.
what_to_bring: Proof of income, ID, proof of address.

name: IDNYC (free city ID)
offers: Free photo ID card for anyone in NYC age 10+. Accepted at city agencies, libraries and many banks.
hours_notes: Book an appointment online or call 311 and say "IDNYC". Some sites take walk-ins.
eligibility: Anyone in NYC 10+, regardless of immigration status, record or homelessness.
what_to_bring: Documents worth 3 points for identity and 1 for residency (see the IDNYC document calculator).

name: GetCoveredNYC (health insurance help)
offers: Free help choosing and applying for health insurance, including Medicaid and the Essential Plan.
hours_notes: Call 311, or text CoveredNYC (SeguroNYC in Spanish) to 877877.
eligibility: Anyone, regardless of immigration status or income.

name: HEAP (heating bill help)
offers: Help paying heating and utility bills, including emergency help if heat is about to be shut off.
hours_notes: NYC applications: 212-331-3126.
eligibility: Low-income households; more help for homes with children under 6, adults 60+ or people with disabilities.
what_to_bring: Proof of income, a utility bill, ID.

name: Aging Connect (help for older adults)
offers: The city's line for older adults and caregivers: home-delivered meals, older adult centers, caregiver support, legal help.
hours_notes: Weekends: call 311. Older adult centers are free for anyone 60+.

name: NY State Unemployment Insurance
offers: File or ask about an unemployment claim.
hours_notes: You can also file at dol.ny.gov.
eligibility: People who lost work through no fault of their own.
what_to_bring: Social Security number, employer names and addresses, dates worked.

name: DYCD Community Connect
offers: Free referrals to youth programs, afterschool, summer jobs, teen parenting classes, youth drop-in centers and family services.
hours_notes: From outside NYC: 646-343-6800.
eligibility: Young people up to 24 and their families.

name: CUNY Adult Literacy Program
offers: Free English (ESOL), pre-HSE and HSE/GED classes at 14 CUNY campuses in all five boroughs. Day, evening and weekend classes.
hours_notes: Find a campus on the CUNY site, then contact that program. Many have waitlists.
what_to_bring: Photo ID.

name: NYPL free English classes
offers: Free English conversation classes (We Speak NYC), series classes and citizenship prep at libraries in the Bronx, Manhattan and Staten Island, plus online classes.
neighborhood: Bronx, Manhattan, Staten Island and online
hours_notes: In-person conversation classes need no registration. Online classes need sign-up.

name: Housing Court Answers hotline
offers: Free information about Housing Court, tenant rights and rent arrears help, with referrals to free lawyers. Information tables in each housing court.
hours_notes: Interpreters available.
what_to_bring: Court papers.

name: Legal Services NYC Access Line
offers: Free civil legal help for low-income New Yorkers: eviction, benefits, family, debt, immigration, disability.
hours_notes: For new callers.
what_to_bring: Any papers about your case.

name: NYLAG (New York Legal Assistance Group)
offers: Free civil legal help: immigration, benefits, housing, family, consumer debt, and more.
hours_notes: New clients: call Mondays and leave a message, or email ipuintake@nylag.org.

name: Legal Aid Society civil helpline
offers: Free civil legal help for low-income New Yorkers: housing, benefits, immigration, employment, family.
hours_notes: Main number: 212-577-3300.
to_confirm_on_call: Is this helpline still active (older listing)?
